iris/labels/labels.json (partial read: metadata + pass1 source labels)
metadata.independence: Triage verdicts derive solely from reading the real source at each codeFlow step and an empirical guard-behavior test run locally (CPython pathlib relative_to with '..' segments: no ValueError; absolute replacement: ValueError; single leading './' strip only). No PyVul ground-truth files, no CVE advisories and no fix patches on disk were opened. The fix-commit data used for the second task (ground_truth_hit_analysis) is the metadata pasted into the task prompt by the operator, used only for the coverage cross-check, never for the per-alert verdicts.
metadata.sarif_content_check: The SARIF contains exactly one run, tool 'CodeQL', one rule (py/augur/py7zr/pass1-path-traversal) and 13 results, all of that ruleId. No diagnostics results, no CodeQL built-in security queries, and no other CWE rules are mixed into this Pass 1 formal result set.

shared_analysis.untrusted_boundary: py7zr is a library + local CLI with no HTTP surface. The attacker-controlled input is the archive CONTENT: (a) entry names, UTF-16LE-decoded from the 7z header PROPERTY.NAME block at py7zr/archiveinfo.py:757 (read_utf16 defined at archiveinfo.py:192-200) with backslash->slash rewrite at the same line; (b) link-target payload bytes, decompressed from the archive stream and read at py7zr.py:1333 (junction) / :1343 (symlink). Anyone who can feed a crafted .7z to SevenZipFile(..., 'r'), .extractall()/.extract()/.read(), unpack_7zarchive (shutil.unpack_archive hook), or `py7zr x` controls these values. No authentication applies to archive content.
shared_analysis.allowed_root: The declared extraction base is the caller-supplied `path` argument of extractall/extract (CLI --odir) — all 13 realized codeFlows run the path-is-not-None branch (py7zr.py:582 joinpath base) — or os.getcwd() in the path=None branch (:577/:580, not realized in any alert flow).
shared_analysis.guard_evidence: 1) py7zr.py:583-586 `outfilename.relative_to(path)` -> ValueError -> Bad7zFile, and py7zr.py:576-579 (cwd variant): LEXICAL prefix checks. CPython pathlib keeps '..' as literal parts, so Path(base).joinpath('../../tmp/evil.sh').relative_to(base) returns '..\..\tmp\evil.sh' WITHOUT raising (empirically re-verified locally); only absolute-path replacement / different drive raises. The guards run before every sink but do not neutralize '..' traversal. 2) helpers.py:424-433 remove_relative_path_marker strips exactly one leading './' (RELATIVE_PATH_MARKER='./', helpers.py:38); '../../x' survives. 3) py7zr.py:596-597 WindowsPath('\\?\'+...) prefixes absolute survivors (win path-length workaround, not a filter). 4) py7zr.py:562-568 '_%d' suffixing is name-collision handling. 5) NO resolve(), realpath(), normpath, basename mapping, fixed-name mapping or whitelist exists anywhere between the decode (archiveinfo.py:757) and the file accesses. 6) The link-target channel (:1333/:1343 -> :1338/:1347) is never seen by ANY guard — dst/sym_target are decompressed raw bytes passed unvalidated.
shared_analysis.flow_carrier_evidence: py7zr.py:619/:621 self.worker.register_filelike(f.id, outfilename) -> py7zr.py:1500-1502 self.target_filepath[id] = fileish (real dict store) -> Worker.extract invoked at py7zr.py:635-644 (possibly via Thread/Process, py7zr.py:1240-1259) -> py7zr.py:1320 fileish = self.target_filepath.get(f.id, None) inside Worker._extract_single. The dict is populated before extract() is called, so the concurrency wrapper does not break the data flow; the SARIF threadFlows compress the :619->:1320 hop (site-anchored summary edge) but both endpoints and the carrier store are real code, independently verified. No fabricated interprocedural step was found.
shared_analysis.irreport_discrepancy: iris_report.md's automated filter marked all 13 findings 'Likely FP' via the regex guard heuristic (reject|deny|block.*\.\.), presumably keying on the Bad7zFile raise / 'invalid directory traversals' comment near py7zr.py:570-586. This independent path review OVERRIDES that automated verdict: the guard exists but is ineffective against '..' segments (verified above), so every alert describes a genuinely escaping path. The report's heuristic conflates presence-of-check with effectiveness-of-check.

sink.operation: target_dir.mkdir(parents=True) — directory tree creation at attacker-influenced path (SevenZipFile._extract post-pass over target_dirs)

alerts.taint_flow: :561 outname = f.filename -> :582 outfilename = path.joinpath(remove_relative_path_marker(outname)) -> :612 target_dirs.append -> :623 sorted -> :625 mkdir receiver
alerts.preconditions: extractall/extract called with a `path` argument; entry has is_directory attribute; outfilename does not already exist (:611).
alerts.rationale: Real directory-creation sink; '..' entry names pass the lexical relative_to guard at :584 (verified), so a crafted archive creates directories outside the caller-declared base. Match comment/summary is accurate.

sink.operation: os.utime(str(outfilename), times=(lastmodified, lastmodified)) — timestamp write on extracted path (post-extract metadata pass)

alerts.preconditions: path argument given; entry is a regular file (reaches :621/:622); properties['lastwritetime'] present (attacker controls it); worker extraction completed without raising.
alerts.rationale: utime is a genuine filesystem write (metadata modification) on the escaping path; usually secondary to the :1349 write but independently realizable (e.g. empty-stream entries with target_files registration, or post-write). str() coercion is value-preserving.

sink.operation: outfilename.chmod(st_mode) — permission change with archive-supplied posix_mode

alerts.preconditions: os.name == 'posix'; properties['posix_mode'] not None (archive-supplied); regular-file entry; path argument given.
alerts.rationale: Platform-gated but real: chmod on a path outside the base (attacker additionally controls the mode). Prefix/lexical guards do not stop it.

alerts.preconditions: properties['readonly'] true and not is_directory; non-posix or posix_mode None; regular-file entry.
alerts.rationale: Same escaping-path chmod on the Windows/non-posix fallback branch; mode bits derived from the existing file, path still entry-controlled.

sink.operation: fileish.open(mode='wb') followed by self.decompress(..., obfp, ...) — THE Zip-Slip arbitrary-file-write sink (Worker._extract_single): creates/truncates the target file and writes attacker-controlled decompressed content

alerts.taint_flow: :561 -> :582 joinpath -> :621 register_filelike(f.id, outfilename) -> (dict store :1502) -> :1320 fileish = self.target_filepath.get(f.id) -> :1349 receiver fileish
alerts.preconditions: path argument given; entry is a non-empty regular member (not directory/socket/symlink/junction, emptystream false); not a return_dict MemIO extraction.
alerts.rationale: Both the write location (entry name, weakly guarded) and the written bytes (decompressed payload) are attacker-controlled. This is the direct realization of 'write arbitrary files via extracting a crafted 7z file' — the core CWE-22 of this project. No effective barrier on the path.

sink.operation: symlink creation at attacker-chosen location (link-location channel)

alerts.preconditions: entry flagged is_symlink (archive-supplied attributes, py7zr.py:174-182); not MemIO; path argument given.
alerts.rationale: The link is planted at a location that can sit outside the base ('..' in entry name passes the guard). Even with a benign target, a misplaced link enables later symlink-following writes (CWE-23/36 escalation).

sink.operation: symlink creation with attacker-chosen TARGET (link-target channel)

source.origin: omfp.read() over decompressed archive bytes (io.BytesIO fed by self.decompress at :1341)

alerts.preconditions: entry flagged is_symlink; non-empty payload; not MemIO.
alerts.rationale: Zero validation between the raw payload read and symlink_to: the target may be absolute (e.g. /etc/passwd) or a '../../' chain — the relative_to guards never inspect it at all. CWE-36-shaped arbitrary link target.

sink.operation: fileish.unlink() — file deletion at attacker-chosen path (symlink branch pre-collision clobber)

alerts.preconditions: entry flagged is_symlink; a file/dir already exists at the escaping path (fileish.exists() at :1345); not MemIO.
alerts.rationale: Deletion (or clobber of an existing link) outside the declared base; TOCTOU window between exists() and unlink()/creation is a documented residual risk but does not negate the path-escape itself.

sink.operation: fileish.touch() — empty-file creation at attacker-chosen path

alerts.preconditions: entry has emptystream true (0-byte member); not a MemIO extraction; path argument given.
alerts.rationale: touch creates/truncates nothing but creates the file node at the escaping path (and updates mtime if present) — real filesystem mutation on an uncontained path.

sink.operation: fileish.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) — directory tree creation for every extracted member (Worker._extract_single)

alerts.preconditions: any member with a registered target (all non-None registrations); runs before every write/link/creation below.
alerts.rationale: Unconditional per-member mkdir of the parent chain; with '..' in the entry name this materializes directory trees outside the base before any file write.

sink.operation: fileish.unlink() — file deletion at attacker-chosen path (junction branch)

alerts.preconditions: entry flagged is_junction (archive attributes, py7zr.py:184-191); sys.platform == 'win32'; not MemIO; fileish.exists() at :1335.
alerts.rationale: Windows-gated deletion/clobber outside the base; same weak entry-name containment.

sink.operation: NTFS junction creation at attacker-chosen link path (link-location channel)

alerts.preconditions: entry flagged is_junction; sys.platform == 'win32'; not MemIO; non-empty payload.
alerts.rationale: Windows-only branch, but statically real: the junction is planted at the (weakly guarded) entry-name location. Combined with A-13 the attacker controls BOTH ends of the junction.

sink.operation: NTFS junction creation with attacker-chosen TARGET (link-target channel)

source.origin: ofp.read() over decompressed archive bytes (io.BytesIO fed by self.decompress at :1332)

alerts.preconditions: entry flagged is_junction; sys.platform == 'win32'; non-empty payload.
alerts.rationale: The junction target is raw archive payload with no validation whatsoever — an absolute path or arbitrary directory can be aliased from inside the extraction tree (CWE-36). Windows-gated only.

checklist_answers.1_source_attacker_controlled: Yes — not URL/route input but the project's genuine untrusted boundary: archive entry names (archiveinfo.py:757, UTF-16 decode of header PROPERTY.NAME bytes) and link-target payload bytes (py7zr.py:1333/:1343, decompressed stream). Fully attacker-controlled whenever a crafted .7z is supplied to the read/extract APIs (library, shutil.unpack_archive hook, CLI).
checklist_answers.2_source_reaches_sink: Yes — every codeFlow step was checked against real source: :561/:565 outname -> :582 path.joinpath(remove_relative_path_marker(outname)) (helpers.py:424-433 strips only one leading './') -> :612/:613/:619/:621 registration -> target_filepath dict store (py7zr.py:1500-1502) -> :1320 load in Worker._extract_single -> sinks. The thread/process wrapper (Worker.extract, py7zr.py:1240-1259) does not sever the flow: the carrier dict is populated before extraction starts. The SARIF :619->:1320 hop is a compressed but code-backed edge.
checklist_answers.3_sink_is_real_file_operation: Yes — all 13 sink sites are genuine operations: mkdir (:625, :1328), os.utime (:659), chmod (:663, :668), unlink (:1336, :1346), open(mode='wb')+write (:1349), touch (:1357), symlink_to (:1347), _winapi.CreateJunction (:1338). None are pure concatenation or path-object construction.
checklist_answers.4_allowed_root_and_escape: Declared base = caller `path` (extractall/extract/CLI --odir) or os.getcwd() (path=None branch). Controlled entry names escape via '..' segments: pathlib keeps them literally, so joinpath('..\..\x') stays under-concatenated and the OS resolves it outside the base at access time. Empirically re-verified locally that relative_to does not raise for this shape.
checklist_answers.5_traversal_vectors: Effective: '..' chains (survive both relative_to guards and remove_relative_path_marker); separator variation (backslash names are normalized to '/' at the decode boundary, archiveinfo.py:757, widening reach on posix); absolute link targets and junction targets (payload channel — never checked). Caught: absolute-path replacement / different drive (relative_to raises -> Bad7zFile). Not applicable: URL/percent decoding, repeated decoding (no second decode exists). Symlinks: created by the extractor itself with unchecked targets (CWE-23/36 pivot).
checklist_answers.6_effective_guards_before_access: None effective. The relative_to checks (py7zr.py:576-579, :583-586) do run before access but are lexical; no resolve/realpath/normpath/basename/whitelist exists anywhere in the pipeline; link-target values bypass all checks entirely.
checklist_answers.7_misjudged_barrier: No — this review explicitly does NOT credit relative_to/joinpath as sufficient (they are the vulnerability), and there is no login/auth to misjudge. The IRIS report's automated FP filter did exactly this misjudgment (regex heuristic crediting the Bad7zFile raise); overridden here with source-level and empirical evidence.
checklist_answers.8_not_authorized_static_service_or_test: These are not static-file-serving, test or unreachable paths: the alerts are on the core extraction pipeline of a library whose input (the archive) is untrusted by design. Only platform/attribute preconditions apply (win32 gates at :1330/:1338; posix gate at :660; is_symlink/is_junction/emptystream flags — all attacker-chosen via archive attributes).
checklist_answers.9_fp_from_overgeneral_modeling: No evidence: sources and sinks are site-anchored to real lines; the DB covers helpers.py (flows traverse helpers.py:424-433); no wrapper-parameter sources were promoted; sink positions carry real path text. The 4 duplicate threadFlows per result are the two source anchors (561/565) x two route variants (direct / via helpers.py) — not spurious distinct claims.
checklist_answers.10_no_contamination: Confirmed: single ruleId py/augur/py7zr/pass1-path-traversal, 13 results, no diagnostics and no CodeQL built-in baseline results present in the SARIF.

ground_truth_hit_analysis.task: Cross-check whether the real vulnerability fixed by py7zr commit 1bb43f17515c7f69673a1c88ab9cc72a7bbef406 (CWE-22 path traversal, extractall arbitrary file write) is hit by the Pass 1 formal alerts. Basis: the commit metadata pasted in the task prompt (code_before/code_after for writef, _extract_single, _extract, extract, writestr) + the alert set above. No on-disk ground-truth files were opened.
ground_truth_hit_analysis.overall_verdict: HIT (extraction channel fully covered; write-side channel NOT covered)

function_level_mapping.fix_nature: Replaced the weak relative_to containment (:576-586 in code_before) with get_sanitized_output_path() built on resolve()-then-relative_to; removed the windows-namespace prefixing path.
function_level_mapping.evidence: The vulnerable code_before lines are exactly the alert flow steps: outname = f.filename (:561), outfilename = path.joinpath(remove_relative_path_marker(outname)) (:582), the bypassed relative_to guard (:583-586), register_filelike (:619/:621), and the sinks target_dir.mkdir (:625), os.utime (:659), chmod (:663/:668). Alerts A-01..A-05 traverse precisely the pipeline this commit rewrites; the commit's own message ('resolve() converts /hoge/fuga/../../../tmp/evil.sh to /tmp/evil.sh then relative_to() can detect') matches this review's empirical finding that the pre-fix guard keeps '..' literally.

function_level_mapping.fix_nature: Added is_target_path_valid(path, fileish.parent.joinpath(dst)) checks before junction creation (:1338) and symlink creation (:1347), raising Bad7zFile on out-of-target link targets; junction/symlink branch hardening.
function_level_mapping.evidence: Alerts anchor exactly at the changed sink sites: junction unlink/CreateJunction (:1336, :1338 arg0, :1338 arg1 = dst), symlink unlink/symlink_to (:1346, :1347 receiver, :1347 sym_target), plus the shared extraction machinery (:1320, :1328, :1349, :1357). The unvalidated dst (:1333) and sym_target (:1343) flows are precisely what is_target_path_valid was added to block.

function_level_mapping.fix_nature: Plumbing: passes `path` through extract() into extract_single() so the new link-target validation can run.
function_level_mapping.evidence: Covered as the (compressed) carrier segment of every Worker-sink alert flow (:619/:621 register_filelike -> :1320 target_filepath.get inside the extract/extract_single call chain), not as a standalone sink — appropriate, since the function itself only dispatches.

function_level_mapping.fix_nature: Added check_archive_path(arcname) guard rejecting evil arcnames such as '../../../../tmp/evil.sh' on the archive-CREATION side (writef code_before at :671+ / writestr at :920+ in the vulnerable tree).
function_level_mapping.evidence: No Pass 1 alert touches writef, writestr, _writef, _writestr or _make_file_info_from_name. This is by construction of the Pass 1 labels: all write-side rows were deliberately left 'candidate' (operator-supplied arcname, not archive content) and no write-side source/sink was promoted. The write-side is a hardening addition in the same commit rather than the extractall CWE-22 channel itself, but it is a real uncovered fix surface.

ground_truth_hit_analysis.coverage_of_primary_cve: The primary vulnerability ('directory traversal in SevenZipFile.extractall() ... write arbitrary files via extracting a crafted 7z file') is directly hit: A-05 (py7zr.py:1349 fileish.open(mode='wb') + decompress write) is the arbitrary-file-write sink of that exact scenario, reached from the archive entry-name source through the exact guard the commit replaced. Twelve companion alerts cover the adjacent manifestations the same commit fixed (directory creation, deletion, metadata writes, and the junction/symlink target escapes).
residual_coverage_gaps: path=None branch (extractall() without a path, read(), readall(); pipeline :577/:580 against os.getcwd()) is modeled as source/joinpath but no realized alert flow traverses it — same root cause, same fix, minor recall gap only.
Write-side hardening (writef/writestr check_archive_path) has no alert at all.
Binary-level quirks (e.g. absolute entry names on Windows drive-relative forms, UNC paths) are covered by neither alerts nor this review beyond the relative_to absolute-rejection test.
